original_value: In real life, human opinion cannot be limited to yes or no situations as shown in an ordinary fuzzy sets and intuitionistic fuzzy sets but it may be yes, abstain, no, and refusal as treated in Picture fuzzy sets or in Spherical fuzzy (SF) sets. In this article, we developed a comprehensive model to tackle decision-making problems, where strong points of view are in the favour; neutral; and against some projects, entities, or plans. Therefore, a new approach of covering-based spherical fuzzy rough set (CSFRS) models by means of spherical fuzzy    β   -neighborhoods (SF    β   -neighborhoods) is adopted to hybrid spherical fuzzy sets with notions of covering the rough set. Then, by using the principle of TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution) to present the spherical fuzzy, the TOPSIS approach is presented through CSFRS models by means of SF    β   -neighborhoods. Via the SF-TOPSIS methodology, a multi-attribute decision-making problem is developed in an SF environment. This model has stronger capabilities than intuitionistic fuzzy sets and picture fuzzy sets to manage the vague and uncertainty. Finally, the proposed method is demonstrated through an example of how the proposed method helps us in decision-making problems.

result.paraphrase: Human opinion is not restricted to simple yes/no choices, as in ordinary fuzzy sets and intuitionistic fuzzy sets; it may instead be yes, abstain, no, or refusal, as in picture fuzzy sets or spherical fuzzy (SF) sets. In this article, we develop a comprehensive model for decision-making problems in which views may be in favor of, neutral toward, or against projects, entities, or plans. Accordingly, we adopt a new covering-based spherical fuzzy rough set (CSFRS) approach using spherical fuzzy β-neighborhoods (SF β-neighborhoods) to combine spherical fuzzy sets with rough-set covering notions. We then apply TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution) to spherical fuzzy data, presenting the TOPSIS method through CSFRS models based on SF β-neighborhoods. Using the SF-TOPSIS methodology, a multi-attribute decision-making problem is formulated in an SF environment. This model has greater capability than intuitionistic fuzzy sets and picture fuzzy sets for handling vagueness and uncertainty. Finally, an example demonstrates how the proposed method supports decision-making problems.
